hypotheses.paper: (4.87): ∂0 + Σ δi ∂i timelike for g(u1,du1) for all Σ|δi| < δ
hypotheses.note: CurveNestedOn (slopeCone E δ hδ) C U₁ ∨ CurveNestedOn (slopeCone E δ hδ) C.dual U₁: the graphs of δ-Lipschitz maps in U₁ (the curves of the static cone of slope δ around ∂₀) are causal curves of U₁ for C, future-directed, or past-directed (C.dual). This is the binder's reading of (4.87) (binder.toml erslem:PropertyTimelike note); the smooth step from 'the vectors of the open cone are g-timelike' to 'the Lipschitz graphs of the closed cone of slope δ' < δ are C_g-causal curves' is not formalised. The disjunction is the paper's 'without loss of generality ∂0 is future directed' (ghd_02_19.tex:1160): one time orientation on U₁, which (4.87) gives when U₁ is connected, as it is under the paper's connected S.

hypotheses.paper: R^{d+1} with the ℓ¹ cone Σ|δi| < δ
hypotheses.note: ℝ × E, E any real normed space (any dimension, any norm); the paper's ℓ¹ cone is E = WithLp 1 (Fin d → ℝ) (checked: ers_lemma_4_86_oneSidedBoundary applies to it, /tmp check), the closed cone of any δ' < δ.

hypotheses.paper: conclusion (4.83): a chart ψ : V → (−ε,ε)^{d+1}, f continuous, ψ⁻¹(graph f) = ∂U1 ∩ V, below ↦ U1, above ↦ R^{d+1} ∖ U1
hypotheses.note: BoundaryGraph U₁ (closure S): at p ∈ ∂U₁ ∖ closure S, LiesBelowGraphAt U₁ p (p.1 > 0) or LiesBelowGraphAt (flipT⁻¹' U₁) (flipT p) (p.1 < 0): a cylinder V = (t₀−ε, t₀+ε) × B_E(x₀, ρ), f continuous on B_E(x₀, ρ) with values in (t₀−ε, t₀+ε), inside V: z ∈ U₁ ↔ z.1 < f z.2 and z ∈ ∂U₁ ↔ z.1 = f z.2 (so above the graph is outside U₁). The chart is the translation by −p, composed with (t,x) ↦ (−t,x) when t₀ < 0. For E = Fin d → ℝ (sup norm) the base is a cube of side 2ρ; reaching the paper's cube (−ε,ε)^{d+1} needs a linear rescaling of space, not formalised. Moreover f is 1/δ-Lipschitz (exists_lipschitz_graph_of_cone).
closure S, as OQ-41 (e); proved immaterial when S ⊆ U₁ (frontier_diff_closure_eq_frontier_diff_edge, ers_lemma_4_86_edge for the edge reading closure S ∖ S).

findings: ghd_02_19.tex:1160, 'It thus follows that t_0 ≠ 0': not a consequence of p ∉ ∂S alone; it needs U₁ ∩ {x⁰ = 0} ⊆ S and more: a boundary point of U₁ on {x⁰ = 0} is a limit of points of U₁, whose vertical projections lie in S (the vertical line through a point of U₁ meets S, by the Cauchy property), so it lies in closure S. Proved as the t₀ = 0 case of Causal.ers_lemma_4_86_future through Causal.proj_mem_of_curveNestedOn; the argument is causal (uses (4.87) and the Cauchy property), not topological.

ghd_02_19.tex:1162 (and footnote): the 'past directed and past inextendible timelike curve in U₁ starting at q ∈ I⁺(S, U₁)' needs, in ETT, a two-sided inextensible curve (DEC-11/13) and no extension principle is available for an abstract C_g. The formal proof takes the maximal piece in U₁ of the whole straight line of slope ≤ δ, inextensible at both ends with no CurvesExtend and no antisymmetry (Causal.Causality.inextensible_connectedComponentIn); the footnote's case distinction (q in the future of S) disappears: the piece meets S, at time 0, so the line stays in U₁ between q and {x⁰ = 0} (Causal.slopeLine_mem_of_curveNestedOn).

ghd_02_19.tex:1168, the sequential continuity argument for f⁺ can be replaced by a bound: |f⁺(x) − f⁺(y)| ≤ ‖x − y‖/δ on a ball (Causal.exists_lipschitz_graph_of_cone), f⁺ is 1/δ-Lipschitz, stronger than the continuity (4.83) asks.
ghd_02_19.tex:1168, typo: '(x^0, f^+(\underline{x})) ∉ U_1 for x^0 ≥ f^+(\underline{x})' should read '(x^0, \underline{x}) ∉ U_1'.

The proof uses only that S is met by every inextensible causal curve of U₁ (not uniqueness, not global hyperbolicity), S ⊆ {x⁰ = 0} (not open, not connected), any norm on space and any dimension: Lemma 4.86 holds in that generality (Causal.ers_lemma_4_86).
questions: (4.87) is read as the closed slope-δ cone (any δ' below the paper's δ) curve-nested in C_g on U₁, with either time orientation (C or C.dual). This is the binder's reading; the smooth step is T-pkg-smooth-lorentz. Is it the formalisation of record for (4.87)?

(4.83) is read in the identity chart (translation, time reflection below {t = 0}), V a cylinder (t₀−ε, t₀+ε) × B_E(x₀, ρ); the paper's cube (−ε, ε)^{d+1} is its image under a linear rescaling of space, not formalised. Accept this as (4.83)?
∂S read as closure S (OQ-41 (e)): shown immaterial when S ⊆ U₁ (both readings give the same set). The question can be closed for this lemma.
Whether the readings above (layer-3 translation of (4.87) and of the Lorentzian Cauchy hypersurface, DEC-14) suffice to mark erslem:PropertyTimelike: I did not mark it.
